claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi-based alloys are high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys.
An AlCoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy will show a more gradual ductile–brittle–ductile transition than conventional steels.
An AlCoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy will show less severe embrittlement than conventional steels.
The proposed initial alloy is as-cast and homogenized.
The proposed alloy has a predominantly BCC/B2 or FCC-containing microstructure.
The proposed alloy has minimal segregation.
The range from 250 to 600 °C is characteristic of temper embrittlement in steels.
A stable multi-principal-element solid solution mitigates grain-boundary segregation.
A stable multi-principal-element solid solution mitigates short-range-ordering effects associated with embrittlement in simpler alloys.
Compositional complexity and lattice distortions distribute solute atoms more uniformly at grain boundaries.
More uniform grain-boundary solute distributions suppress embrittling interfacial phases or segregation.
Suppressing embrittling interfacial phases or segregation preserves ductility across the embrittlement-prone temperature range.
Conventional alloys can exhibit an approximately 50–70% reduction in impact energy during temper embrittlement.
The proposed HEA will retain comparatively greater ductility throughout the embrittlement window.
The proposed HEA will recover full ductility above the embrittlement window.
High-strength steels typically suffer a pronounced ductility decrease after exposure to approximately 250–600 °C.
Processing routes or compositions that cause excessive precipitation or segregation may degrade the alloy's ductility.
Maintaining a stable, compositionally complex matrix is necessary for preserving ductility.
